title: Protect maximum HP and commit to a coherent deck plan
situation: When offered the five-Bite transformation or later card rewards after the deck already has a functional core.
lesson: Treat the Bite-for-max-HP exchange as a strong default refusal unless a special enabler such as Blood Vial makes the healing substantially better. More broadly, identify an archetype early—such as exhaust or status—and skip rewards that do not improve that plan once the deck is serviceable.
evidence_points: Act 2 Floor 19 accepted removal of all Strikes for five Bites and lost 24 maximum HP, leaving a 56-HP ceiling.
The final deck had 30 cards, including five Bites and many separately chosen attacks, defensive cards, and exhaust pieces rather than a tightly focused package.
The run repeatedly took Act 2 damage and reached the Champ with only 35/56 HP in the combat summary; the final relic list contained no Blood Vial.
reasoning: The Bite event imposed a permanent health penalty while adding a large group of similar attacks, and continued card additions made the deck less consistent. A focused plan with more skipped rewards would improve draw quality and preserve the HP margin needed for Act 2 and the boss.

title: Use Armaments+ proactively before spending the hand
situation: When Armaments+ is in hand, especially before playing several attacks or defensive cards and when multiple cards can benefit from an upgrade.
lesson: Use Armaments+ early in the turn in most situations, regardless of whether the enemy is attacking or defending, unless a specific immediate lethal or survival line is clearly stronger. Upgrading the rest of the hand first improves the value of the cards played afterward.
evidence_points: Armaments was bought on Act 1 Floor 2 and later upgraded, producing Armaments+ in the final deck.
In the Act 2 Floor 25 Gremlin Leader fight, the logged sequence played Shockwave+, Bite, and other actions before playing Armaments+ later in the combat.
The final deck contained multiple upgrade-sensitive cards, including Bash+, Uppercut+, Pommel Strike+, Fiend Fire+, Hemokinesis+, and Shockwave+.
reasoning: Playing other cards before Armaments+ can forfeit upgrades on the cards already used and reduce the card's value for the turn. Since this deck had many impactful upgrade targets, treating Armaments+ as an early setup card would generally produce more damage, block, or utility over the combat.

title: Do not route to shops without enough gold for essential help
situation: When gold is low or when a shop is competing with safer route options and its available purchases are not necessary to avoid imminent death.
lesson: Preserve gold for a meaningful combat solution—such as an essential potion, defensive card, or removal—and avoid visiting another shop when unable to afford one. At low HP, a shop is justified when it can directly prevent death, not merely because purchases are available.
evidence_points: At the Act 2 Floor 29 shop, the run had 19/56 HP and spent 373 gold on removal, Centennial Puzzle, Hand Drill, and True Grit, leaving only 47 gold.
The same run then visited another shop on Floor 31 with 47 gold and spent 24 on Pommel Strike, despite having no potions afterward.
The final Champ combat began with only 35/56 HP in the combat summary, so the shop spending did not create a large immediate survival margin.
reasoning: The shop sequence converted a large gold reserve into several long-term purchases while the urgent constraint was surviving upcoming fights. If a low-gold shop cannot provide a necessary answer, skipping it preserves route flexibility and avoids spending resources on marginal additions to an already oversized deck.

title: Do not pass on legal defense at critical HP
situation: When HP is extremely low, an enemy is attacking, and a block card can be played with remaining energy.
lesson: Prioritize survival by playing available block rather than ending the turn. At 4 HP, even a modest Defend is generally more valuable than preserving energy when the alternative is taking an incoming attack.
evidence_points: On Turn 6 of the final fight, HP was 4/77, Block was 0, Energy was 1, and the hand contained two Defends.
Donu had Intent ATTACK, and Play Defend was a legal alternative, but the chosen action was End turn.
reasoning: This was a direct, avoidable survival error: usable defense and energy were available against an attacking enemy. The run survived the immediate turn but remained critically fragile and ultimately lost the boss fight.

title: Stop adding marginal attacks once the deck has a core
situation: After establishing an exhaust-and-draw engine and acquiring enough damage, especially when the deck is already large.
lesson: Skip redundant or marginal card rewards unless they materially improve the deck's plan. Preserve access to key setup, draw, defense, and exhaust cards instead of continuing to add attacks that dilute consistency.
evidence_points: The final deck had 38 cards, including three Perfected Strikes, two Carnages, two Uppercuts, two Headbutts, two Sword Boomerangs, and two Corruptions.
Late in Act 3, the run continued adding Perfected Strike, Pummel, Dark Embrace, Sword Boomerang+, and Shrug It Off rather than consistently skipping rewards.
reasoning: The deck had a functional Corruption, Burning Pact, True Grit, and Dark Embrace shell, but its size and repeated attack packages reduced the chance of drawing the most important cards at the right time. Once damage is sufficient, selectivity generally improves reliability more than further attack additions.

title: Take profitable curse events only with immediate removal available
situation: When an event offers substantial gold for taking a curse and the route provides a near-term shop with enough funds for removal.
lesson: Convert the event into net value only when removal is realistically available soon. Reserve the required gold and remove the curse promptly rather than allowing its ongoing downside to dilute the deck.
evidence_points: Act 1 Floor 2 accepted 175 Gold and gained the Doubt curse, increasing gold from 109 to 284.
At the Act 1 Floor 3 shop, the run paid 75 gold for card removal and selected Doubt.
reasoning: The run turned the curse event into a substantial economic gain while preventing Doubt from remaining in the deck. This event-and-shop sequence is a reusable pattern when the route and finances support immediate cleanup.
